ux_rules.do: Use scroll-behavior: smooth on html element
Add padding-top to body equal to nav height
ux_rules.dont: Let nav overlap first section content

ux_rules.do: Highlight active nav item with color/underline
ux_rules.dont: No visual feedback on current location

ux_rules.do: Use for sites with 3+ levels of depth
Animate 1-2 key elements per view maximum

ux_rules.dont: Use animations longer than 500ms for UI
Leave UI frozen with no feedback
Rely only on hover for important actions

ux_rules.do: Use transform and opacity for animations
Use ease-out for entering ease-in for exiting
Test all content fits within containers
Account for safe areas and other fixed elements
Understand what creates new stacking context
ux_rules.dont: Expect z-index to work across contexts

ux_rules.do: Use dvh or account for mobile browser chrome

ux_rules.dont: Let text span full viewport width

ux_rules.do: Avoid horizontal swipe on main content
Use for confirmations and important actions
Use visible focus rings on interactive elements
Change cursor and add subtle visual change
ux_rules.dont: No hover feedback on clickable elements

ux_rules.do: Disable button and show loading state
Show clear error messages near problem
Show success message or visual change
Use icons/text in addition to color
Descriptive alt text for meaningful images

ux_rules.dont: Skip heading levels or misuse for styling
Keyboard traps or illogical tab order

ux_rules.do: Use semantic HTML and ARIA properly
Use label with for attribute or wrap input
Use aria-live or role=alert for errors
Provide skip to main content link
ux_rules.dont: No skip link on nav-heavy pages
